description:
pkix-profiles/src/lib.rs:222-223 — SmimeProfile sets:
  `p.max_validity_secs = Some(1185 * 86_400);`

In pkix-path chain_walk, max_validity_secs is checked for EVERY certificate in the chain (comment at line 2051: 'Applies to every cert in the chain per the epic intent'). This means intermediate CA and root CA certificates with validity periods greater than 1185 days (~3.25 years) will be rejected when using smime_policy.

CA/B Forum S/MIME BR §6.3.2 sets the validity cap specifically for subscriber (end-entity) certificates. Root and intermediate CA certificates in S/MIME hierarchies routinely have validity periods of 10-20 years.

Using smime_policy() with a chain that has a typical CA hierarchy (e.g., 10-year intermediate) will fail with ValidityPeriodExceedsMax on the intermediate cert, even though the S/MIME BR cap applies only to end-entity certificates.

This is the same issue as CodeSigningProfile: the max_validity_secs field applies to all chain members. The correct approach would be to only enforce the cap on the leaf cert.

P2 — SmimeProfile and CodeSigningProfile cannot be used with typical CA hierarchies that have long-lived CA certificates.
title: pkix-profiles SmimeProfile: max_validity_secs applies to ALL certs; CA certs may exceed 1185 days
